description: Table 7 is a single-image table (no axes, curves, scale bars, micrographs or schematics in the group) titled "σ at two strain levels using different α values at RT". It has three printed column headers — α, Engineering strain (%), and σ_diff (MPa) — and six data rows, fully legible: α = 0.136 gives σ_diff = 152 MPa at 10 % and 280 MPa at 20 % engineering strain; α = 0.26 gives 88 MPa and 146 MPa; α = 0.40 gives 15 MPa and 25 MPa. Reading the table shows two consistent trends: at each fixed α, σ_diff rises when strain goes from 10 % to 20 %, and at both strain levels σ_diff falls monotonically as α increases from 0.136 through 0.26 to 0.40. The smallest discrepancy in the table is therefore the pair of α = 0.40 values (15 MPa and 25 MPa). The table is the evidence panel behind the paper's choice of α for the flow-stress model of the Fe35Mn6Al0.1C austenitic steel: the citing text states that σ_diff is the difference between the experimentally measured stress (σ_exp) and the modelling stress (σ_mod) computed with Eq. (20), that the three α values tested are commonly used values (0.136, 0.26, 0.4), and that α = 0.4 gives the smallest σ_diff, justifying α = 0.4 in the subsequent dislocation/twinning flow-stress calculation. No experimental conditions other than "at RT" are printed inside the table.

subfigures.description: A six-row, three-column table whose headers are α, Engineering strain (%) and σ_diff (MPa). Rows: 0.136/10/152; 0.136/20/280; 0.26/10/88; 0.26/20/146; 0.40/10/15; 0.40/20/25. All cells legible; no other graphical elements are present.

observations.observation: The table's three printed column headers are α, Engineering strain (%), and σ_diff (MPa).
The table contains six data rows covering two engineering strain levels (10 % and 20 %) for each of three α values (0.136, 0.26, 0.40).
At α = 0.136, σ_diff is printed as 152 MPa at 10 % engineering strain and 280 MPa at 20 % engineering strain.
At α = 0.26, σ_diff is printed as 88 MPa at 10 % engineering strain and 146 MPa at 20 % engineering strain.
At α = 0.40, σ_diff is printed as 15 MPa at 10 % engineering strain and 25 MPa at 20 % engineering strain.
σ_diff decreases monotonically as α increases from 0.136 to 0.26 to 0.40 at both the 10 % and 20 % strain levels, so the smallest tabulated discrepancies are the α = 0.40 pair (15 MPa and 25 MPa).
For every α value, σ_diff at 20 % engineering strain is larger than σ_diff at 10 % engineering strain.
The caption states that the tabulated σ values were obtained at room temperature (RT) using different α values.
The citing text states that σ_diff is the difference between the experimentally measured stress (σ_exp) and the modelling stress (σ_mod), calculated by Eq. (20).
The citing text states that three commonly used α values are compared: 0.136, 0.26, and 0.4 (with references [64], [37,73] and [63] respectively).
The citing text asserts from Tables 7 and another table that when α is 0.4 the σ_diff is the smallest among the three commonly used α values.
The citing text states that for austenite the parameters used are M = 3.06, α = 0.4, G = 68 GPa, b = 0.26 nm, with dislocation density ρ taken from Table 3.
The citing text states that the ferrite contribution to flow stress is very minimal, less than 10 MPa, so ferrite is neglected and flow stress is calculated for a fully austenitic structure.
